title: Section Placement
description: Directs code and data sections to specific memory areas - fast RAM for hot code, flash for constants - through linker script rules. Precise placement is how embedded systems fit in tiny memories and hit timing targets.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Memory Regions
description: Declares named memory regions - FLASH, SRAM, CCM - with origins and lengths that sections then target. Regions make the script readable and let one script serve board variants by changing only region definitions.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Entry Points
description: Sets the program entry point symbol where execution begins after reset, typically the reset handler. A correct entry point is the difference between a booting board and a dead one.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Symbol Versioning
description: Tags exported symbols with version nodes so libraries can evolve their ABI without breaking old binaries. Versioning lets one shared library serve programs built against several of its past releases.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Overlay Sections
description: Overlays multiple sections at the same runtime address, loading each on demand - the classic technique for fitting big programs in small memories. Overlays trade manual management for fitting where nothing else fits.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Linker Relaxation
description: Lets the linker shrink instructions - long jumps to short ones - once final addresses are known, saving space and cycles. Relaxation recovers the pessimization that position-independent code would otherwise impose.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Garbage Collection Sections
description: Discards unreferenced sections at link time when each function lives in its own section, trimming dead code automatically. Section GC is the embedded developer's best friend for fitting in flash.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Alignment Control
description: Forces section alignment to cache lines, page boundaries, or DMA requirements through script directives. Correct alignment prevents performance cliffs and hardware faults on strict-alignment architectures.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: PROVIDE Symbols
description: Defines symbols like _sdata and _edata only if the program does not, giving startup code reliable boundaries for initialization. PROVIDE is how the C runtime finds where to copy initialized data and zero the BSS.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Map File Analysis
description: Reads the linker's map file to verify section addresses, sizes, and symbol placement against the intended memory map. Map analysis is the final check that the script did what the datasheet required.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Script Validation
description: Lints linker scripts for common errors - overlapping regions, undefined symbols, misordered sections - before they produce subtly broken binaries. Validated scripts turn linker mysteries into clear build errors.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Multi-Region Layouts
description: Spreads sections across several memory regions - internal flash, external RAM, tightly-coupled memory - matching each section to the memory that suits it. Multi-region layouts extract maximum performance from heterogeneous memories.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Bootloader Handoff
description: Arranges the image so the bootloader can verify and jump to the application - vector table first, checksums where expected. Handoff layouts are a contract between two programs that must agree exactly.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Scatter Loading
description: Describes load versus execution addresses separately so code runs from RAM while stored in flash - the ARM scatter-loading model. Scatter files give fine control over the copy-from-flash-to-RAM dance at startup.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Script Linting
description: Applies style and correctness linting to linker scripts themselves - unused regions, magic numbers, missing comments. Linted scripts stay maintainable as boards and memories evolve across product generations.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
